sections.html: Kaysville is a Davis County city in the Ogden-Clearfield area, with Layton to the north, Fruit Heights to the east and Farmington to the south. It covers 10.54 square miles. The 2020 count found 32,945 people in 8,958 households, and only 2.4% of the 9,175 housing units stood vacant. On a street where almost every house is occupied, a neglected or empty one stands out fast.

Hector Haight came north in 1847 looking for feed for livestock. The settlement later honored William Kay, who became bishop of the local ward in 1851. It was first called Kay's Ward. Residents once asked to rename it Freedom, and Brigham Young answered, 'When did Kay's Ward get its Freedom.' The name stuck. Kaysville was incorporated on March 15, 1868, the first city in Davis County. The history is a talking point, but buyers today care far more about the roof, the permits and the price.

Davis County is a bedroom community, and many residents drive to Salt Lake County. Hill Air Force Base, up in the northern part of the county, employs nearly 23,000 military and civilian workers and is the biggest single employer. Other big employers include the Davis School District, Lagoon Amusement Park and Lifetime Products.

  • Relocating for work? Ask any buyer to put the closing date in writing.
  • A house you must vacate before a move can go as it stands, without staging.
  • Heirs in other states can finish a sale through a title company and never set foot in town.

Kaysville students attend Davis School District schools, and Davis High is the local high school. The city supplies garbage pickup, curbside and green waste recycling, power, pressure irrigation, storm water and water. Sewer comes from Central Davis Sewer and not from the city. Kaysville City Power is at 721 W Old Mill Lane, phone 801-544-8925.

sections.h2: Building permit fees and expired permits
sections.html:
Kaysville prices permits by project value, then adds a 1% state education fee and a 25% plan check fee. The city posts a fee schedule online, along with impact fees for building a new house.

Permit or feeKaysville amount
Parks and recreation impact fee, new home$4,480
Central Davis Sewer fee, new home$2,400
North Davis Sewer fee, new home$3,454.03
Basement finish or remodel permit$245.70
Furnace, A/C or water heater permit$65.65
Pool permit$260 plus a $500 bond

Work that never starts within 180 days, or sits idle for 180 days, kills the permit and costs you the construction bond. Say your half-finished basement carries a dead permit. A lender-backed buyer may demand it be closed out, while a cash buyer can take the house as it is and deal with the permit later.

sections.h2: Renting part of your Kaysville house
sections.html:
The city permits internal accessory dwelling units under Kaysville City Code 17-31-3, with one condition: the owner has to occupy either the main house or the unit as a primary residence.

  • Renting to anyone outside the family triggers a permit requirement.
  • Paved parking for the unit is separate from the two-car garage and two-car driveway.
  • Detached structures, such as an apartment over a garage or a granny flat, cannot be lived in.
  • Additions or remodels that create the unit need a building permit.

Bought a house that comes with a basement apartment? Verify that it was built to these rules. A house rented out entirely, apartment included, may not qualify because the owner must live there.

Valuation notices leave the Davis County offices at the end of July. The appeal cutoff under Utah law is whichever comes later, September 15 or 45 days after the auditor's notice, so phone Tax Administration for the exact date before filing.

Only market value is appealable, never the rate. County commissioners sit as the Board of Equalization and rely on hearing officers they appoint. Bring closing documents, a certified appraisal or comparable sales. An agent who files for you needs notarized authorization.

  • The Tax Administration office is in Farmington at 61 South Main Street, Room 101.
  • Phone: 801-451-3331 or 801-451-3329.
  • Late appeals can be heard by the board when circumstances are extenuating.

Under the primary residential exemption, a qualifying home is taxed on just 55% of market value. That status does not carry over, so warn the buyer that a new application is due after closing.
A bill still open at closing comes out of your proceeds, with the year divided between you and the buyer. Request the proration number early so your net payout holds no surprises.

sections.h2: How a cash sale closes in Kaysville
sections.html:
Closing happens at a title company, and the Davis County Recorder files the deed. Without a loan the sequence is short: purchase contract, title search, signed settlement statement, recording.

Utah requires the deed to name the grantees, show a mailing address for assessment and tax purposes, and carry a legal description that meets state standards. Expect the recorder to ask for the parcel's tax identification number as well.

There is no mortgage underwriting, so nothing hangs on a lender's appraisal, and no bank-driven repair list stands between you and the closing table. You do not stage rooms, host open houses or schedule strangers through the home. The offer is based on the house as it is today, and you pick the closing window that fits your move, whether that is quick or a few weeks out.

The steps stay simple and few. You share the address, we review the property and nearby sales, you accept or decline, and the title company handles the search, the signing and the filing at the county.

This is a young, family-oriented city, with a median age of 29.9 and 52.4% of households raising children under 18. An empty house after a move or a death looks out of place, and the carrying costs keep running.

  • Inherited houses needing updates before they could list.
  • Basement apartments set up without a permit or without the required parking space.
  • Expired building permits with a forfeited bond.
  • Owners who must relocate and cannot manage showings from afar.

Whatever you choose, work out the net after repairs, commission and holding costs, and read every contract before signing.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html: Gather the deed, the newest tax notice, permits for any finished basement or remodel, and paperwork on a basement apartment. Jot down your utility providers as well: the city handles water, power and pressure irrigation, but sewer is separate. With these at hand, the title office needs less back and forth.

faqs.q: What is the property tax appeal deadline in Davis County?
faqs.a: The cutoff is the later of September 15 or 45 days after the notice. Call Tax Administration at 801-451-3331 for the exact date.

faqs.q: Can I put an apartment in my Kaysville basement?
faqs.a: Yes, as an internal accessory dwelling unit, provided you live in the house or the unit. Add a paved parking space of its own, and get a permit if the tenant is not family.

faqs.q: Who provides sewer service in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Central Davis Sewer provides sewer service, not the city. The city provides water, power, pressure irrigation, garbage, recycling and storm water.

faqs.q: Do building permits expire in Kaysville?
faqs.a: Yes. Work that does not begin within 180 days, or halts for 180 days, ends the permit. You lose the bond and must apply again.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kaysville?
faqs.a: About 32,945 at the 2020 count, with an estimate of 33,307 for July 1, 2025.
